summary: Autonomism is a far-left, anti-authoritarian Marxist current that grew in 1960s-70s Italy and treats working-class struggle, not capital's development, as the motor of history. It rejects party and union mediation and the state, expands the working class to the whole 'social factory' of precarious, student, domestic and migrant labour, and favours direct action, refusal of work, a social wage and horizontal self-organisation. Post-operaist writers such as Hardt and Negri carry this into a global politics of the multitude, exodus and absolute democracy, and the German and wider European Autonomen apply the same autonomy to squats, anti-fascism and anti-imperialism.
scope: Italian operaismo (Panzieri, Tronti, Negri) and autonomia (Potere Operaio, Autonomia Operaia), the 'autonomist Marxism' Cleaver names after them (s7), and post-operaismo (Hardt and Negri's Empire and Multitude, s3), plus the German and wider European autonomous movement, the Autonomen of the squats, black bloc and anti-imperialist struggles in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark and Switzerland, which Geronimo (s5) and Katsiaficas (s6) present as the same autonomia carried north. Katsiaficas notes the German movement is not Negri's workerism (s6) and that 'autonomist' is not a German term for it (s6, note on usage), so strands differ. Autonomist feminism (Dalla Costa, Wages for Housework) is a variant. Excludes the Leninist party tradition and armed-party groups (RAF, Red Brigades) as organisations, though some Autonomen moved toward them.
